messages:
Morgan: Quick sync — planning private deploy roadmap for H2. Field feedback centers on two hard things: upgrades with near-zero downtime, and customer-managed networking (peering/firewall constraints). Who can help scope launch criteria and the minimal ops surface?

Jules: I'll own upgrade orchestration design. Thinking a lightweight coordinator agent + a ledger to track per-host state. Targets: rolling upgrades with a 5–7m observed window for a 20-node pool. Need to nail drain semantics.

Rachel: NetOps notes: customers expect 2-way TLS for control plane, explicit SNI routing for multi-tenant gateways, and a published port/IP list. We can't assume customer will open ephemeral ranges — they want pinned IPs and docs for NAT traversal.

Ada: From CS: lots of regulated customers are asking to opt out of auto-upgrades entirely or have a manual approval step. They also need audit logs for each agent action (who kicked the upgrade, what version, timestamps).

Sam: Sales input: we need an easy presales checklist and a clear rollback story. If we say "private deploy upgrades supported" in our enterprise pitch, we must have a documented rollback plan and an SLA for problematic upgrades.

Jules: Proposal sketch: two upgrade modes — "orchestrated-rolling" (default) and "operator-controlled" (manual). Agent exposes a drain endpoint and a state machine: PENDING -> DRAINING -> UPGRADING -> VALIDATING -> ACTIVE. We'll add a fenced feature flag so customers can opt-out. Example config snippet for agent control: 

```yaml
agent: 
  mode: orchestrated-rolling # or operator-controlled
  drain_timeout: 300s
  max_surge: 1
  allow_auto_upgrade: false # customer-settable
```

Jules: Also plan to keep an immutable upgrade ledger stored at /var/lib/rw-upgrade/ledger.log for audit and rollback.

Kai: Runtime note: when we change kernel/quantization combos we must include a compatibility matrix and a fallback kernel. Add a model-compat flag to the agent so it can refuse an upgrade if runtime incompat. That reduces risk for serving regressions.

Rachel: Networking handshake flow we recommend: 1) Customer provisions TLS cert (or CSR flow we support), 2) Customer whitelists control plane IPs (we publish a CIDR list), 3) Customer configures SNI mapping if they run multiple clusters, 4) Optionally enable hole-punch for NATs. We'll need docs + a troubleshooting checklist with tcpdump commands and sample iptables rules.

Ada: Telemetry constraint: customers require only metrics and health metadata — no request/response payloads. Add an explicit "telemetry_level: metrics_only" flag and KMS/HSM notes for key material.

DeployBot: deployment queued: staging-upgrade-2026-06-05 by @Jules.

Morgan: Launch gates (draft): 
- Gate 1: Canary run on a dedicated internal cluster with automatic rollback on health regression.
- Gate 2: 3 pilot customer on-prem upgrades completed with <10m downtime and successful rollback tested.
- Gate 3: NetOps checklist and published IP/port + CSR flow doc.
- Gate 4: Presales one-pager and rollback runbook completed.

Rachel: I'll author the IP/port doc and NAT hole-punch guide. ETA 2026-04-06.

Jules: I'll deliver the upgrade spec (state machine, ledger, agent APIs, sample configs) by 2026-03-30 and wire up canary job.

Ada: I'll recruit 3 pilot customers and draft the audit requirements by 2026-04-10.

Sam: I'll draft the presales checklist and rollback one-pager; need an example rollback command and expected RTO.

Morgan: Action items captured. Final ask: everyone add a concrete test scenario to the spec (happy path, kernel mismatch, network blackhole, manual abort). We'll reconvene next Tue. :thumbsup:
